customer tier, and nobody wants to add a fourth copy of the block.

   - tax rates live in one module-level dict `TAX_RATES` mapping category to rate, with the

content.text:
I refactored `pricing.py` and added the gold tier. `python3 test_pricing.py` passes all four tests.

- **Module-level tables:** `TIER_DISCOUNTS` (silver 0.05, gold 0.12, platinum 0.20) and `TAX_RATES` (books and food 0.07, with `"default"` at 0.19).
- **`price_line(item, customer)`:** returns the `{"sku", "net", "tax"}` dict, or `None` when qty is at most 0. It applies the bulk discount before the tier discount, as the original did.
- **`checkout`:** keeps its signature and coupon logic. It now builds lines through `price_line`.

To confirm "exactly the same results", I ran the original and refactored `checkout()` side by side on 200,000 random carts, customers, and coupons. Results and exception types matched every time. Gold was left out of that run, since it is new behaviour. I checked gold separately: a 10-unit line at 3.33 comes to 26.37 net, which is the expected 12% off after the bulk discount.

Two choices to review:
- The original code had no safe way to look up unhashable values such as a list `tier` or `category`, which would have raised `TypeError`. A small `_lookup` helper treats those as "no match", as the old `==` chain did.
- I kept the file's `# DO NOT TOUCH` header comment, since it is still the file's history. You may want to change it now that the code has been refactored.

The directory is not a git repo, so there was no commit.
